Exteriors — sky, weather, fog and ground#

A villa, a tower, a street: an exterior needs a sky over it, ground under it and, when the pitch calls for it, weather. The exterior kit (2.7) adds all three to any scene, on every device, without a recompile.

What you get#

FeatureWhat it doesWhere it works
Physical skyA daylight dome (Preetham model) placed by the Sun panel: noon is blue, evening warm, the horizon hazes with turbidity. Its light also fills live-lit surfaces (the ambient follows the sun). A procedural cloud layer with coverage and density scrolls with the wind.WebGPU and WebGL2. Baked (lightmapped) scenes keep their bake and only get the backdrop.
WeatherRain streaks or snowflakes falling around the visitor; rain also wets upward-facing surfaces (darker, glossier).WebGPU and WebGL2 (wet response: streamed scenes on both, classic GLBs on WebGPU).
FogHeight fog — dense at a chosen height, thinning above — in a colour of your choice.WebGPU and WebGL2.
GroundA grass / asphalt / sand / custom-coloured plane under and around the model, sun-shadowed, fading to the horizon; or a heightfield (a PNG you upload) with real relief. Walkable: visitors stand on it.WebGPU and WebGL2.

Try it in a link#

Every knob is a share-string, so you can preview without saving:

Code
/?vpk=ingest/<id>.vpk&sun=140,25,3&sky=3,1,0.4,0.6
/?vpk=ingest/<id>.vpk&sky=2.5&weather=rain,0.7,2&fog=0.02,0,8fa3bf,0.2
/?vpk=ingest/<id>.vpk&sky=4,1,0.8,0.7&weather=snow,0.5,1&ground=grass,120
KnobValues
sky=turbidity,exposure,coverage,density[,atmosphere[,aerial]] — turbidity 1 (alpine) … 10 (hazy), exposure around 1, cloud coverage and density 0–1. A bare sky turns it on with defaults; sky=0 off. The optional atmosphere picks the clear-sky atmosphere model instead of Preetham (deeper blue overhead, a thin pale horizon, warm glow round the sun, warm sunlight); aerial (0–8, 1 = clear air) then hazes distance the way real air does. Big exteriors (township-scale sites) open with atmosphere,1 by default.
weather=rain|snow|none,intensity,windX[,windZ] — intensity 0–1, wind in m/s.
fog=density,height,rrggbb[,falloff] — density 0.005 (a hint) … 0.1 (thick), height in metres, falloff how fast it thins above. fog=0 off.
ground=grass|asphalt|sand|rrggbb,size[,y] — size in metres (default 60), y the ground height (default: just under the model). ground=none off. Heightfields come from the saved experience, not the link.

The Sun panel's ?sun= sets where the sun is; the sky follows it.

Author it and save it#

  1. Open the scene as its owner with ?author=1 (a signed-in Studio session). Beside Sun in the toolbar there is Exterior.
  2. Sky — tick on, drag turbidity (crisp → hazy), exposure, clouds. Move the sun in the Sun panel and watch the dome and the ambient follow.
  3. Weather — pick rain or snow, set intensity and wind. Rain darkens and polishes floors and roofs; walls stay dry.
  4. Fog — tick on, set density, the height it sits at, how fast it thins, and its colour.
  5. Ground — pick plane, a material and a size; leave Height y empty to sit just under the model. For relief, pick a PNG (≤ 4096 × 4096, the red channel is the height, white = Relief metres up), press Upload, and the kind switches to heightfield. Click Walk — you are standing on it.
  6. In the Author bar tick **Save the exterior (sky, weather, fog, ground) with this experience, press Save, then Set as link default**. The plain share link now opens with your exterior; the link also carries the knobs while you work, so a copied URL previews the same look.

The heightfield lives beside the scene as ingest/<id>.ground.png (API: PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/ground, SDK: scenes.setGround) and follows the scene's visibility and version rules.

Embeds#

Code
const viewer = Verse.embed(el, { scene: "<id>", exterior: { sky: "3,1,0.4,0.6", ground: "grass,120" } });
viewer.on("exterior", (e) => console.log(e.state.sky, e.query));
viewer.setExterior({ weather: { kind: "rain", intensity: 0.6 } });
viewer.setExterior(null); // everything off

Good to know#

  • Baked scenes. A lightmapped scene keeps its own light; the sky is a backdrop there, and the ground is still lit live. For a sky-lit look, bake with the sun you want, or upload the live-lit file.
  • Interiors. Rain and snow fall through roofs (the sheet has no collision) — leave weather at none inside, or use fog alone.
  • Clouds are a 2D layer: they move and light with the sun but cast no shadows on the ground.
  • Ground is one square; it receives the sun's shadow but casts none, and it fades to the horizon rather than ending at an edge.
  • WebGL2 draws everything; its classic-GLB meshes (not streamed scenes) skip the wet response.
  • Values are clamped engine-side; a link with a junk knob still renders.

Gate: web/test/fix-verify-exterior.mjs (ports 8870–8879).
